gen_risks.description: High exclusion and inclusion targeting errors persist in existing safety net programs, leading to misallocation of social assistance funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate proxy means testing (PMT) objective scoring modules in the Dynamic Social Registry (DSR) and incentivize targeting of the poorest two quintiles via PBC 5.
gen_risks.evidence: Exclusion and inclusion errors remain a challenge... Nearly half (47 percent) of the poor households are not covered by any social assistance program.

gen_risks.description: Technical failures, lagging MIS development, or data synchronization errors during DSR implementation, reflecting lessons from past National Household Database efforts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor DSR in existing ISPMIS linked directly to NID/BRN databases, establish dedicated technical implementation units at FD and DSS, and utilize national data centers.
gen_risks.evidence: Past efforts to create a social registry through the National Household Database (NHD) did not materialize due to incomplete and outdated data, lag in management information system.

gen_risks.description: Data security breaches or unauthorized access to sensitive personal socio-economic data stored within the DSR and linked MIS platforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adhere to national data security regulations, implement robust data encryption protocols during module design, and enforce data security standards in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: To ensure strong standards of data protection through the collation and collection of data for Component 1, GoB will adhere to its national data security regulations.

gen_risks.description: High ongoing inflation erodes the real purchasing power and adequacy of cash allowance benefits provided to poor beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and adopt a standardized, index-linked benefit adequacy framework (PBC 3) to conduct periodic evidence-based reviews of allowance levels for MoF budgeting.
gen_risks.evidence: Inflation remained elevated, reaching 9.9 percent in January 2025... the real value of benefits under the DSS’s Old Age Allowance and Widow Allowance programs has decreased.

gen_risks.description: Shortfall or delayed release of Government of Bangladesh counterpart financing (US$ 3,848 million) required for cash transfer program allocations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure explicit annual budget line provisions in iBAS++ under the Development Project Proforma and maintain close supervision via the DSR Steering Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Total Operation Cost 4,048.00... Counterpart Funding 3,848.00... early cuts in government funding.

gen_risks.description: Financial management complexity across multiple implementing agencies and diverse funding flows (grants, stipends, operating costs) leading to reporting errors or disbursement lags.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint experienced FM consultants at both PIUs, integrate iBAS-PMAP for automated accounting and IUFR generation, and conduct independent annual internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: From the FM perspective, the project design is complex due to the intricacy of activity selection and various IAs and finances.

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling key legal covenants and institutional setups, such as establishing PIUs and adopting the Project Operations Manual within specified months.
gen_risks.mitigation: Begin advance preparation of ToRs and POM guidelines, draw experienced staff from prior World Bank projects, and conduct regular task team compliance reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall establish within six (6) months of the Effective Date... PIU at DSS... POM within six (6) months.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing DSR access points and completing staff training across all sub-districts (Upazilas) within scheduled project timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy standardized training modules early through field social workers and Union Digital Centers, tracking progress through floating PBC 4.4 and 4.5 targets.
gen_risks.evidence: Each Upazila in the country has at least one DSS personnel who has been trained... Each Upazila... has at least one access point.

gen_risks.description: Gender-based barriers, low digital/financial literacy, and mobility constraints preventing poor women from enrolling in DSR and livelihoods programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement simplified local-language audio guides, conduct proactive field outreach, deliver financial literacy training, and enforce a 50% target for female livelihoods beneficiaries.
gen_risks.evidence: The gender gaps derive from several underlying barriers... women report limited digital and financial access, which constrains their access to G2P payments.

gen_risks.description: Physical, social, and logistical accessibility barriers preventing persons with disabilities (PWDs) and the elderly from benefiting from social care services and shelters.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish age- and disability-inclusive local social clubs, provide higher training stipends for PWDs, and build union/Upazila referral networks for physical and psychosocial care.
gen_risks.evidence: Women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities (PWDs) report limited access to resources... mobility constraints... shelters lack the necessary accessibility features.

gen_risks.description: Institutional disruptions or policy momentum slowdown resulting from the ongoing political transition and macroeconomic uncertainty in Bangladesh.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor high-level administrative governance in the Cabinet Division Steering Committee and execute formal binding MoUs between Finance Division, DSS, and line ministries.
gen_risks.evidence: An interim government was sworn in on August 8, 2024... Real GDP growth is projected to decline in FY25... affected by significant uncertainties due to recent political transition.

gen_risks.description: Recurring extreme weather events, severe flooding, and cyclones disrupting physical operations, in-person training, and field data collection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate e-learning options for training, host MIS platforms in data centers equipped with disaster recovery facilities, and utilize digital G2P payment networks.
gen_risks.evidence: recurring flooding affects a greater share of the population... A major flood in August 2024 affected over 3 million people... risk of intense floodings... restrict in-person attendance.

gen_risks.description: Lack of administrative integration, shared data, and coordinated management across DSS's four distinct livelihoods programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated livelihoods coordination team within the DSS PIU, harmonize program MIS systems, and update unified livelihoods program operational guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: These programs are part of a single ecosystem... However, there is limited integration within these programs in terms of administrative systems, data/information, and resource management.

gen_risks.description: Broader economic slowdown, energy shortages, and informal sector constraints hampering post-training wage employment and self-reliance for program graduates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide bundled economic inclusion support (productive grants, skill training, stipends, and market linkages) informed by rigorous local market assessments.
gen_risks.evidence: Slowdown in GDP growth was primarily driven by the industry sector... due to energy shortages, import restrictions, and monetary tightening.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is Substantial. Safety and security concerns persist, despite the priority placed by the interim government on law and order. The interim government is implementing critical reforms before holding elections; reaching a consensus on reforms and the announcement of the election date could heighten political tensions among political parties and the interim government.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated during implementation through continuous engagement with all relevant government and nongovernmental entities, and dialogue with other stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is Substantial. Downside risks have increased, related to uncertainties in the political process and the security situation which affects the recovery of economic activities. The financial sector remains vulnerable with deviations from international regulatory and supervisory standards and weak corporate governance. Despite recent improvements, the balance of payments remained in deficit and FX reserves remained under pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: The macroeconomic risks are partially mitigated by the GoB's reform program, supported by International Monetary Fund arrangements, as well as ongoing World Bank and other development partners' policy lending. Data show consistent budgetary and political commitment to spending on safety nets across regimes in Bangladesh, with strong stakeholder consensus on ensuring a ring-fenced core budget for social assistance and livelihoods programs for the poorest.

gt_risks.description: The Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial due to the involvement of multiple implementing agencies (the DSS and FD), the complexity of activity selection, and intervention modalities. The project's residual procurement risk specifically is also rated Substantial, due to the complexity of procurement activities, multiagency coordination, and capacity limitations (para 56, part of the Fiduciary appraisal-summary discussion immediately preceding the Key Risks section).
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include hiring additional capacity, training, and close monitoring; considering satisfactory implementation of these measures, the residual fiduciary risk is assessed as Substantial and will be managed through proactive and continuous supervision and close dialogue with the GoB. Procurement-specific mitigation: hiring full-time procurement consultants for the DSS and FD; training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, STEP, and contract management; defining clear roles and streamlining approval processes; engaging IT procurement specialists and conducting early market assessments; using performance-based KPIs in contracts and including procurement consultants on bid evaluation committees; and establishing complaint registers at both agencies, with procurement not prior-reviewed by the Bank subject to regular fiduciary reviews and post-procurement review/audit by FAPAD.

gt_risks.description: The project presents a low environmental risk and a moderate social risk, resulting in an overall moderate environmental and social (ES) risk classification. Minor environmental concerns relate to potential e-waste generation from IT equipment and increased energy use. Social risks include potential exclusion of beneficiaries, inadequate consultation, and challenges in reaching remote and marginalized communities, including those who lack IT knowledge; there is also the likelihood of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) cases given the cash transfer modalities of the project and the interaction between service providers and beneficiaries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Waste management protocols and resource efficiency measures will prevent localized pollution. The project will establish a Digital Social Registry (DSR) to improve targeting and coverage, complemented by a robust outreach and monitoring program, and will include Stakeholder Engagement Plan provisions requiring community consultation and disclosure measures. The existing DSS grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will address complaints. An SEA/SH Action Plan will be developed including code of conduct, awareness raising, and GRM to address potential incidents. The project will partially rely on the borrower's ES management framework supplemented by gap-filling measures included in the POM.
